paper_metadata.title: Application of rapid solidification powder metallurgy processing to prepare Cu–Al–Ni high temperature shape memory alloy strips with high strength and high ductility

evidence.quote: Cu–Al–Ni high temperature shape memory alloy (HTSMA) strips were successfully prepared from rapid solidified water atomized Cu–Al–Ni pre-alloyed powders

mechanisms.name: grain boundary pinning by nano-sized alumina particles

evidence.section: 3.3. Microstructural characteristics of finished Cu–Al–Ni SMA strips
evidence.quote: it appears that these nano-sized alumina particles severely pinned the grain boundaries of the recrystallized grains during heat-treatment, leading to a very fine grain size in the heat treated Cu–Al–Ni strips
the growth of the recrystallized grains of plastically deformed water atomized powder particles is inhibited by the alumina particles present inside the original powder particles
the fractured specimens exhibited primarily micro-void coalescence type ductile nature of fracture

the micro-void coalescence type mode of fracture in the present Cu–Al–Ni SMA strips can be attributed to the combined effect of martensitic phase and nano-sized alumina particles inside the matrix, together with small grain size.
